messages.subject: R Shiny - I struggle with working with a selected column name based of an imported .csv file
parts:
I am currently struggling with the following R Shiny problem: In the ui.r the user is able to upload a .csv table which is required for the following analysis. Based on the upload, a select input field is updated which is taking over the column names of the updated table. Now the user is supposed to select the dedicated column from his dataset where the revenue can be found. This column shall then be taken for further calculation processes. So far I succeeded in updating the select input field but I've not yet succeeded in using these names for further steps.

The problem area in the server script is marked with the comment "PROBLEMS". At any position where you can find ...$Revenue, I need to refer to the name from the inputselect-field.

Code excerpt:


UI:

shinyUI (fluidPage(
titlePanel("ABC Analysis"),
sidebarLayout(
sidebarPanel(

fileInput('file1', 'Choose CSV File', accept=c('text/csv', 'text/comma-       separated-values,text/plain', '.csv')),
  selectInput ("rev_col","Choose column with revenue entries",
choices="",    selected=""),))))


Server:

shinyServer( function (session, input, output){

output$str <- renderTable({

inFile <- input$file1

if (is.null(input$file1))

return(NULL)

ABC_Input <- data.frame(read.csv2(inFile$datapath))

updateSelectInput(session, "rev_col", "rev_col", choices = colnames ABC_Input))


#PROBLEMS: HOW TO USE rev_col in the following steps?


#Create new sorted table

Data_new <- ABC_Input[order(ABC_Input$Revenue, decreasing = T),]


#Create cumsum variable

Data_new$Rev_CumSum = cumsum(Data_new$Revenue)


#Create Percentages of CumSum


Data_new$Percent_Rev_Cum <- Data_new$Rev_CumSum / sum(Data_new$Revenue)})



Somehow I need to replace "ABC_Input$Revenue" with "ABC_Input$(input$rev_col)" as the dedicated column name is saved in input$rev_col.


Thanks for your help.


Greg

parts:
I broke the server function down, to untangle it as follows:

1- I made ABC_Input reactive, so that you can track the changes and re-use it.
2- I got observeEvent out of renderTable
3- I made Data_new reactive and outside of renderTable (in case you will re-use it or sth). Inside it, I called ABC_Input()to get the reactive value and then make calculations.
4- I added renderTable at the end, calling Data_new()

In each step, I made sure the required values are available using req(), I might be missing sth, but you can start from here and make your checks.


server <- function (input, output,session){
 
  ## reactive value to read the csv file in ----------
  ABC_Input <- reactive({
    req(input$file1)
    data.frame(read.csv(input$file1$datapath))
  })
 
  ## observe input$file1 to update the input$rev_col ------------
  observeEvent(input$file1,{
    updateSelectInput(session,
                      inputId = "rev_col",
                      choices = names(ABC_Input()))
  }
  )
 
  ## Data_new as reactive (could be used in other chuncks)---------------
  Data_new <- reactive({
    req(input$rev_col)
    # now ABC_Input is reactive, so you need to call ABC_Input()
    Data_new <- ABC_Input()[order(ABC_Input()[input$rev_col], decreasing = T),]
    # Create cumsum variable
    Data_new$Rev_CumSum = cumsum(Data_new[input$rev_col])
    #Create Percentages of CumSum
    Data_new$Percent_Rev_Cum <- Data_new$Rev_CumSum / sum(Data_new[input$rev_col])
   
    return(Data_new)
  })
 
  ## render table of Data_new() -------------------
  output$str <- renderTable({
    req(input$rev_col)
    Data_new()
  })
 
}

parts:
You are welcome. I suggest you take a step back and try the following:

  • Make sure you understand the difference between the reactive expression, which give the recipe of getting a certain value, depending on inputs or other reactive values
    x <- reactive({....})
    and getting it's value at a certain moment using:
    x()

  • Try to write element by element and print the output or try to inspect it to see what you get at each point
  • Break things down
    • If you need to recalculate the same value in different chunks, write the reactive expression once, and reuse it
    • If a block performs many tasks(calculate values, save, render...etc.) , try to break it to multiple blocks
Then it will take less time for you and others to isolate the problem/s.

You are welcome. I suggest you take a step back and try the following:

  • Make sure you understand the difference between the reactive expression, which give the recipe of getting a certain value, depending on inputs or other reactive values
    x <- reactive({....})
    and getting it's value at a certain moment using:
    x()

  • Try to write element by element and print the output or try to inspect it to see what you get at each point
  • Break things down
    • If you need to recalculate the same value in different chunks, write the reactive expression once, and reuse it
    • If a block performs many tasks(calculate values, save, render...etc.) , try to break it to multiple blocks
Then it will take less time for you and others to isolate the problem/s.

Am Dienstag, 7. Februar 2017 11:35:01 UTC+1 schrieb omayma Said:
I broke the server function down, to untangle it as follows:

1- I made ABC_Input reactive, so that you can track the changes and re-use it.
2- I got observeEvent out of renderTable
3- I made Data_new reactive and outside of renderTable (in case you will re-use it or sth). Inside it, I called ABC_Input()to get the reactive value and then make calculations.
4- I added renderTable at the end, calling Data_new()

In each step, I made sure the required values are available using req(), I might be missing sth, but you can start from here and make your checks.


server <- function (input, output,session){
 
  ## reactive value to read the csv file in ----------
  ABC_Input <- reactive({
    req(input$file1)
    data.frame(read.csv(input$file1$datapath))
  })
 
  ## observe input$file1 to update the input$rev_col ------------
  observeEvent(input$file1,{
    updateSelectInput(session,
                      inputId = "rev_col",
                      choices = names(ABC_Input()))
  }
  )
 
  ## Data_new as reactive (could be used in other chuncks)---------------
  Data_new <- reactive({
    req(input$rev_col)
    # now ABC_Input is reactive, so you need to call ABC_Input()
    Data_new <- ABC_Input()[order(ABC_Input()[input$rev_col], decreasing = T),]
    # Create cumsum variable
    Data_new$Rev_CumSum = cumsum(Data_new[input$rev_col])
    #Create Percentages of CumSum
    Data_new$Percent_Rev_Cum <- Data_new$Rev_CumSum / sum(Data_new[input$rev_col])
   
    return(Data_new)
  })
 
  ## render table of Data_new() -------------------
  output$str <- renderTable({
    req(input$rev_col)
    Data_new()
  })
 
}
